text:
Predicates:
Supervised(x) ::: x is supervised learning.
Unsupervised(x) ::: x is unsupervised learning.
Reinforcement(x) ::: x is reinforcement learning.
Labelled(x) ::: x is labelled data.
Train(x, y) ::: x is trained with y.
TextSummarizationModel(x) ::: x is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
MachineLearning(x) ::: x is a machine learning algorithm.
Premises:
∀x (MachineLearning(x) → (Supervised(x) ∨ Unsupervised(x) ∨ Reinforcement(x))) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (Unsupervised(x) → ¬Labelled(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
∀x (MachineLearning(x) ∧ Train(x, TextSummarizationModel(y))) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬Reinforcement(x) ∧ Train(x, TextSummarizationModel(y)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∀x (MachineLearning(x) ∧ Train(x, TextSummarizationModel(y)) → Labelled(x)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
Supervised(x) ∧ Train(x, TextSummarizationModel(y)) ::: Supervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
